project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged vulnerable checkout at `_work/src/freeradius-server` on commit `5776998db7f703188bb85c4a29e691d4e1bb90ef`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. This staged tree still contains the unfixed month parser in `src/lib/util/misc.c` and the unchecked `month_yday[tm->tm_mon]` access in `src/lib/util/time.c`; the saved `patch.diff` names the same `fr_unix_time_from_str()` logic in `src/lib/util/time.c` because later trees moved that helper.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42503442 (freeradius-server): Global-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target fuzzer_util [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42503442
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact 28-byte witness `16 32 34 33 33 2d 31 33 2d 31 31 54 31 37 3a 31 33 3a 31 39 2e 5a 00 c9 00 31 31 23` first makes `util_decode_proto()` read type byte `0x16` (`FR_TYPE_DATE`) and copy the remaining bytes into a NUL-terminated string `2433-13-11T17:13:19.Z`. `fr_value_box_from_str()` therefore dispatches to `fr_unix_time_from_str()`, which parses year `2433`, accepts month digits `13` because the RFC3339 month call is `get_part(..., 1, 13, '-', "month")`, and then decrements that accepted month to zero-based `tm_mon == 12`. The remaining `11T17:13:19` fields and the exact `.Z` suffix are still accepted, so `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` receives a `struct tm` whose month field is 12 and computes `days` with `month_yday[tm->tm_mon]`. `month_yday` has 12 `uint16_t` entries, so index 12 reads one element past the global array; AddressSanitizer reports the saved `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/lib/util/time.c:603:47`. The patch resolves the witnessed path by tightening the month upper bound from 13 to 12 and also adding an extra `tm_mon` check before the later array access.

source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path. It turns the leading attacker-controlled byte into the dispatch key that decides which textual value parser will run.
source.value_from: The exact witness at `gt_results/arvo_42503442/poc` is `16 32 34 33 33 2d 31 33 2d 31 31 54 31 37 3a 31 33 3a 31 39 2e 5a 00 c9 00 31 31 23`. Here `data[0] == 0x16`, which is `FR_TYPE_DATE` in the staged `fr_type_t` enum, so the vulnerable date-parsing path is selected.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the attacker-supplied month becomes the exact out-of-range array index. After step 5 accepts the month digits `13`, this decrement converts that accepted ISO month into zero-based `tm_mon == 12`, which is later used against the 12-element `month_yday` table.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The parser is operating on the copied string prefix `2433-13-11T17:13:19.Z`, so the month substring passed into `get_part()` is exactly `13`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The RFC3339 month parser uses an off-by-one upper bound of 13, so it accepts the singular invalid month `13` instead of rejecting it before `tm_mon` is derived.
root_cause.note: The saved fix tightens this exact bound from `13` to `12`; its additional `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` guard is later defense-in-depth, but the witnessed `tm_mon == 12` path originates here.

sink.code: uint32_t days = 365 * year_adj + leap_days + month_yday[tm->tm_mon] + tm->tm_mday - 1;
sink.description: ASan sink. `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` uses `tm_mon == 12` as an index into the 12-element global `month_yday` array with no bounds check, so the read goes one element past the array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/lib/util/time.c:603:47`, 0 bytes to the right of global `month_yday` (24-byte array of 12 `uint16_t` entries).

parser_admitted.description: By this call the copied payload has already been classified as `FR_TYPE_DATE` and is handed directly into the vulnerable date parser. The saved crash stack contains `fr_value_box_from_str` immediately above `fr_unix_time_from_str`.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` is absent and `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add any instrumentation. The chain is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source, saved ASan traces, `reproduction_report.json`, `patch.diff`, and the staged `poc` bytes.

The staged vulnerable checkout commit (`5776998db7f703188bb85c4a29e691d4e1bb90ef`) differs from the metadata `vulnerable_commit` and from the later file layout shown in `patch.diff`: in this staged tree `fr_unix_time_from_str()` lives in `src/lib/util/misc.c`, while the saved fix hunk shows the same logic after it moved into `src/lib/util/time.c`.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build. `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` is source-grounded from the saved patch text only.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first byte of the exact witness is `0x16`, so `util_decode_proto()` materializes `type == FR_TYPE_DATE`. That attacker-controlled dispatch key is what puts the payload on the date-parsing path instead of another leaf parser.

The remaining 27 bytes are copied into the parser-visible string buffer. For the exact witness, the copied prefix before the embedded NUL is `2433-13-11T17:13:19.Z`; the trailing bytes `c9 00 31 31 23` remain in the buffer but are not consumed by later string parsing.

Because step 1 set the dispatch key to `FR_TYPE_DATE` and `util_decode_proto()` passes `dst_enumv == NULL`, the value parser takes the date case and calls `fr_unix_time_from_str()` on the copied string from step 2.

From the string `2433-13-11T17:13:19.Z`, this parses `tmp == 2433` and leaves `tail` at the first `'-'`. That makes the RFC3339 branch `((tmp > 1900) && (tmp < 3000) && *tail == '-')` true, so `p = tail + 1` points at the attacker month substring `13-11...`.

Root cause. `get_part()` parses the exact month digits `13` and accepts them because this call sets `max == 13`. The parser therefore treats the singular invalid month `13` as admissible input and advances `p` to the day field instead of rejecting the string.
The accepted ISO month is converted to the zero-based `struct tm` month. On the witnessed value, this changes `s_tm.tm_mon` from 13 to 12, which is one past the valid `month_yday` indices `0..11`.

The remaining `11T17:13:19` fields pass their `get_part()` checks. On the exact suffix `.Z`, the subseconds block parses zero digits and leaves `subseconds == 0`, then the `*p == 'Z'` path reaches `done:`. This call forwards the same `struct tm` into `fr_unix_time_from_tm()` without any recheck of `tm->tm_mon`.

fine_trace.code: uint32_t days = 365 * year_adj + leap_days + month_yday[tm->tm_mon] + tm->tm_mday - 1;
fine_trace.note: Sink. `month_yday` is a 12-element `uint16_t` table, but the propagated `tm->tm_mon` value is 12 and the staged vulnerable source has no bounds check before indexing it. This statement therefore reads the first 2 bytes past `month_yday`, matching the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `src/lib/util/time.c:603:47`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Source-grounded only: the saved fix narrows the month parse bound from `13` to `12` and also adds an extra `tm_mon` guard in `fr_unix_time_from_tm()`. The exact witnessed `tm_mon == 12` path is blocked by the parser-side bound fix. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build.

format.contract: Exact 28-byte witness `16 32 34 33 33 2d 31 33 2d 31 31 54 31 37 3a 31 33 3a 31 39 2e 5a 00 c9 00 31 31 23`. Byte 0 must be `FR_TYPE_DATE` (`0x16`), and the zero-terminated payload seen by the crashing parser is exactly `2433-13-11T17:13:19.Z`. The trigger-specific property is the singular month substring `13`, which vulnerable `get_part(..., 1, 13, '-', "month")` accepts before `s_tm.tm_mon--` turns it into out-of-range index 12. Bytes after the embedded NUL are present in the witness but are not consumed by the crashing date parser.
